cold_open.hook: Palo Alto Networks just beat earnings on AI demand while Oracle tanked 5.23%—the market's decided who wins the AI infrastructure race.

markets.macro_note: Broad selloff masks a sharp AI infrastructure divergence; oil strength pushing yields higher, inflation concerns creeping back.

big_story.story_title: Palo Alto Networks beats quarterly estimates on AI demand, continues acquisition spree
big_story.angle: Palo Alto is using AI-driven security demand as a license to print cash and buy competitors—the question is whether they're building a moat or just buying market share at peak valuations.

quick_hits.angle: A major casual dining chain filing Chapter 11 while Denny's stays afloat—labor costs and supply chain pressure are culling the herd, not just consumer weakness.
Google's negotiating with Hollywood studios because AI can't generate original IP yet—the studios have leverage, and Google knows it.
10-year yield hits highest since January as oil prices stoke inflation fears—the Fed's rate-cut narrative just got a lot shakier.
New Apple CEO John Ternus hyping a 'huge launch next week' in his first memo—setting expectations sky-high on day one is either confidence or a trap.

odd_thing.joke_angle: Larry Page's flying car company loses its CEO—turns out the hard part isn't the flying, it's keeping someone in the seat long enough to actually build it.

sign_off.callback_target: Oracle's 5.23% crater—the punchline to Palo Alto's AI win.
